speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I see you've been experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from the gums or other mucous membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. Have you noticed any easy bruising or if your family history includes similar bleeding problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). Given the age of onset, acute presentation with mucosal bleeding, petechiae, and bruising in a child without a family history of bleeding disorders, ITP is the most likely diagnosis. If no response to initial observation is seen or if bleeding worsens, consider a bone marrow biopsy to rule out leukemia or other underlying causes.
